record.title: Radxa ZERO 3W — RK3566 quad-A55 SBC, 40-pin header, 22-pin MIPI CSI, USB-C ×2, Wi-Fi 6 / BT 5.4 (the Microduck's compute board)
record.why: electrical identity and the header/bus map are vendor-cited in iterations/v0.0.1/electrical.host.json (that record's own verdict is PASS). MECHANICAL SIDE CLOSED 2026-09-02: cad/interfaces.json now carries a measured mount-hole frame (4 x Ø2.8140, pitch 57.8429 x 22.8662, edge inset 3.5727 mm, 1 sigma 0.0396 mm) and a measured 40-pin header frame, read off Radxa's §4 raster by tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py with four negative controls PASS; the 'two disagreeing drill patterns' disagree by 0.157 mm along the length and 0.134 mm across (measured), and part.py's RADXA_LONG_SPAN = 54.7 was found to be a misread and corrected. CORRECTED 2026-09-03: this record used to say that disagreement is one 'which an M2.5 screw absorbs'. That was an adjective; tools/check_board_hole_interchange.py did the arithmetic and it is not true in every direction. Over the twelve directions (3 patterns x 2 boards x 2 screw sizes) 9 PASS, 1 CANNOT DETERMINE and 2 FAIL: on M2 every direction passes with 0.2086-0.3676 mm of radial margin, but on M2.5 — the size these Ø2.8140 holes actually take (SPEC.md §4's Ø2.7/2.8 x20 census, docs/BOM.md §4's 'M2.5x6 x20') — a Pi Zero 2 W board on Radxa-pattern posts needs 0.1032 or 0.1414 mm of radial offset where its Ø2.700 hole on a Ø2.500 screw gives only 0.1000 mm. The printed head part must therefore be drilled on the RADXA pattern and a Pi Zero 2 W will not bolt into it on M2.5. cad/interfaces.json mount_holes now records the NOMINAL centres ±28.900 / ±11.400 (Radxa's own printed 3.600 mm inset, the figure this folder already argued was better supported) with the measured ±28.9215 / ±11.4331 beside them, and accepts connection:threaded-m2.5, a folder created in this repo the same day so the field names a ref that resolves. Artifact: out/measure/board-mount-interchange.json. WHAT STILL HOLDS THE VERDICT DOWN: (1) the SKU Pollen fits is still unknown — the store's '1 GB + 32 GB' has no row in Radxa's SKU table, narrowed to two options, and one `lsblk` on a production robot settles it; (2) PCB thickness, corner radius, board mass and which corner is pin 1 are in no Radxa document at all — a calipered board and a scale settle them.
record.origin_why: electrical facts read off Radxa's own product brief (RAD-DOC-0084 rev 1.10), schematics v1.11 and v1.12, and two radxa.com pages, all fetched 2026-09-02 (iterations/v0.0.1/PROVENANCE.json); lifecycle 'active' on the brief's own sentence 'availability … until a minimum date of September 2030' (§8 p.8)
